hero.description: ClickMasters builds production AI-powered search systems that understand what users mean — not just what they type. For enterprises with large document repositories, product catalogs, knowledge bases, or content libraries, the gap between keyword search and semantic search is the gap between users not finding what they need and users getting exactly what they were looking for. sections.title: The search quality problem AI solves
sections.description: Traditional keyword search breaks down when users don't know the exact terminology in the content they're looking for. AI-powered search eliminates this gap.

blocks.heading: Vocabulary mismatch
paragraphs: A user searches 'heart attack' but the relevant documents use 'myocardial infarction.' Keyword search returns no results; semantic search understands these mean the same thing.

blocks.heading: Conceptual queries
paragraphs: 'How do I cancel my subscription?' doesn't match 'subscription termination procedure' or 'account cancellation policy' in keyword search. Semantic search recognizes the conceptual match.

blocks.heading: Long-tail and novel queries
paragraphs: Users rarely repeat the exact phrasing that appears in documents. Semantic search handles the long tail of natural language variation that keyword search can't cover.

blocks.heading: Multi-language search
paragraphs: Cross-language retrieval — searching in English and finding relevant documents in Spanish or German — is natural with multilingual embedding models and impossible with keyword search.

blocks.heading: Product catalog search
paragraphs: Searching 'red dress for wedding guest' should surface relevant dresses across categories, materials, and styles — not just products where the phrase appears verbatim.
AI-powered search eliminates the vocabulary mismatch, handles conceptual queries naturally, and delivers results that match what users mean rather than exactly what they typed.

sections.title: The AI search technology stack
sections.description: The technologies and models that power production AI-powered search systems.

blocks.heading: Embeddings: Converting Text to Searchable Vectors
paragraphs: SBERT (Sentence-BERT) / bi-encoder models: The standard approach for production semantic search. Fast (query encoding takes ~5ms) and scalable. Models: all-mpnet-base-v2, BAAI/bge-large-en, thenlper/gte-large.

Domain-specific fine-tuned models: Fine-tuning a general embedding model on domain-specific training pairs improves retrieval accuracy by 10–25%. ClickMasters fine-tunes embedding models on client-specific domain data.
Multilingual models: paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2 or multilingual-e5-large provide effective cross-language retrieval.

OpenAI Embeddings API (text-embedding-3-large): High-quality embeddings with minimal fine-tuning effort. ClickMasters uses OpenAI embeddings as a baseline and evaluates fine-tuned open-source alternatives.

blocks.heading: Vector Databases: Storing and Searching Embedding Vectors
paragraphs: Pinecone (managed): Leading managed vector database. Serverless option and pod-based option. Best for teams that want managed infrastructure with no operational overhead.
Weaviate (open-source/managed): Strong hybrid search combining vector search with BM25 keyword search built-in. GraphQL API and rich filtering capabilities.
Chroma (open-source, lightweight): Best for development and smaller deployments. Not appropriate for production at scale.
pgvector (Postgres extension): For organizations already running Postgres. Appropriate for smaller document corpora (< 5M documents).
Elasticsearch with vector search: For organizations with existing Elasticsearch infrastructure, enabling hybrid search within a single search system.
FAISS (Meta, on-premise): For on-premise deployments requiring maximum control and minimum infrastructure cost.

blocks.heading: Hybrid Search and Re-Ranking
paragraphs: Hybrid search — combining BM25 keyword retrieval with vector semantic retrieval — consistently outperforms either approach alone. ClickMasters implements hybrid search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

Two-stage retrieval: retrieve a candidate set with a fast bi-encoder, then re-rank with a slower cross-encoder. Cross-encoders: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2, BAAI/bge-reranker-large, or LLM-based re-ranking.

items.question: What is the difference between semantic search and keyword search?
items.answer: Keyword search (BM25/TF-IDF) returns documents containing the query words. Semantic search returns documents with the same meaning as the query, regardless of word overlap. 'Heart attack' matches 'myocardial infarction' in semantic search; not in keyword search. Hybrid search (best of both) typically outperforms either alone.

items.question: Which vector database should I use: Pinecone, Weaviate, or Elasticsearch?
items.answer: Pinecone for managed simplicity and no infrastructure overhead. Weaviate for hybrid search requirements and rich filtering. Elasticsearch for organizations with existing Elasticsearch infrastructure. pgvector for Postgres-native with smaller corpora. ClickMasters recommends based on your specific scale, infrastructure, and filtering requirements.

items.question: How do you improve search quality for my specific domain?
items.answer: Domain-specific embedding fine-tuning on your query-document relevance pairs. If you have historical search data with click-through rates, ClickMasters uses this as weak supervision for contrastive learning. If not, we generate synthetic training pairs using LLMs from your document corpus and fine-tune the embedding model on them.

items.question: How long does AI-powered search development take?
items.answer: Semantic site search: 10–16 weeks. Enterprise document search: 12–20 weeks. Conversational search (RAG): 14–22 weeks. Multimodal search: 14–24 weeks. Timeline is contractually binding from Discovery.

items.question: Can you integrate with our existing Elasticsearch deployment?
items.answer: Yes. ClickMasters adds semantic search capabilities to existing Elasticsearch deployments using Elasticsearch's dense vector type and kNN search — upgrading existing keyword search with semantic capabilities without replacing the entire search infrastructure.
